facts.value: £131m estimate at 31 March 2026, £141m estimate at 31 March 2025, £150m actual at 31 March 2024. All Housing Revenue Account (2012 self-financing). General Fund external debt zero across every year 2023-24 through 2027-28. Expected principal reduction roughly £10m per year

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Indicator 3 table at Section 2.20, page 8. Values in £m: External Debt at 1 April HRA runs 159/150/141/131/121 across the five years; expected change in Debt runs -9/-9/-10/-10/-11; Actual Gross Debt at 31 March runs 150/141/131/121/110. Section 2.43 (page 12) sources the entire external book to March 2012 HRA self-financing: 'The Council borrowed £184m in March 2012 for this purpose with £5m being met by an internal loan. The Council adopted a flexible approach to this borrowing in consultation with treasury management advisers. The outstanding debt as at the 31 March 2024 will be £150m, see 2.20'. No loan-by-loan schedule is printed anywhere in the paper. No LOBO or market debt disclosed. Section 2.7 mentions inter-authority borrowing as a permitted source but no LA-to-LA balance quoted.

facts.value: £182m total at 31 March 2026 estimate (CFR-GF £22m, CFR-HRA £160m); £190m at 31 March 2028 estimate (CFR-GF £40m, CFR-HRA £150m). Section 2.20 (page 8) figures. A second, larger and unlabelled table at Section 1.7 (page 5) shows CFR-style figures of £537.5m total for 2025/26 and £640.9m by 2029/30 — these do NOT reconcile with Section 2.20 and do NOT close the balance-sheet identity; treated as internal-inconsistency for record

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.value: £52m estimate at 31 March 2026 (of which CFR-GF £22m all internal since GF external debt is zero, CFR-HRA £160m minus external £131m = £29m HRA internal). Rises to £81m estimate by 31 March 2028 (CFR-GF £40m + HRA £40m internal), of which £40m sits on the General Fund entirely

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Balance-sheet identity: CFR - external borrowing - OLTL = internal borrowing. For 2025-26: (22 + 160) - 131 - 0 = 51 vs paper's -52 (£1m rounding). For 2026-27: (40 + 156) - 121 - 0 = 75 vs paper's -76. For 2027-28: (40 + 150) - 110 - 0 = 80 vs paper's -81. Identity closes to £1m rounding across all forecast years. OLTL is not separately disclosed but Section 2.24's Authorised Limit table only shows borrowing GF/HRA, implying OLTL is nil or included. Section 2.40 flags the under-borrowed stance explicitly: 'This strategy is prudent as treasury management investment returns are low and counterparty risk is still uncertain.' Financing table at Section 1.3 shows Internal Borrowing of £94.2m (2025/26), £49.6m (2026/27), £38.0m (2027/28), £24.5m (2028/29), £27.7m (2029/30) with External Borrowing at zero across every year — those are the annual financing decisions on the capital programme, not the balance-sheet position.

facts.value: Not disclosed as a numeric loan-count or balance in the paper. Section 2.32 sets an Upper Limit AND Lower Limit both at 31% for the 'Up to five years' bucket for 2026/27 — implying about £40.6m of the £131m estimated at 31 March 2026 sits inside five years, but the paper does not break this into inside-one-year vs 1-5 years

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Section 2.32 Indicator 9 on page 11 sets Upper Limit = Lower Limit for every bucket: Up to five years 31%/31%; 5-10 years 44%/44%; 10-20 years 23%/23%; 20+ years 2%/2%. Highly unusual — most councils write a wide band; equalising upper and lower removes discretion for the S151 to shift the profile during the year without going offside. Not stated whether the values describe the current profile or a target.

facts.value: General Fund: -16% (2023-24 actual), -22% (2024-25 estimate), -26% (2025-26), -19% (2026-27), -16% (2027-28) — negative throughout, meaning investment income exceeds debt service on the GF. Housing Revenue Account: 38%, 38%, 41%, 44%, 46% — rises steadily as the amortisation charge climbs even though HRA external debt is falling

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Section 2.31 Indicator 8, page 11. Section 2.30 (page 10) defines 'financing costs' as 'interest paid, interest and investment income and amounts required for the statutory provision of debt (including repayments of principal, interest and MRP).' The HRA rise is driven by principal-amortisation cash charge climbing as more debt reaches its scheduled maturity each year, not by new borrowing. HRA financing costs in £m under Indicator 7: 12.3 / 13.3 / 14.3 / 15.3 / 16.4 — steady +£1m/yr against HRA gross debt falling 150 / 141 / 131 / 121 / 110.

facts.value: Refinancing maturity structure of borrowing (upper/lower, from Section 2.32 for 2026/27): Up to five years 31%/31%; Five years and within 10 years 44%/44%; 10 years and within 20 years 23%/23%; 20 years and above 2%/2%. Upper equals lower at every bucket — no discretion

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Section 2.32 Indicator 9, page 11. Distinctive stance in the library — most councils write wide bands (Canterbury's for example runs 0% - 50% on the closest bucket). Setting upper = lower means any drift breaches BOTH the upper and lower limits simultaneously. Deliberate on a book that is largely a single 2012 settlement pool. Read as a stance to note, not something to challenge.

facts.value: Authorised Limit (Indicator 4): £110m GF + £188m HRA = £298m total, flat across 2023-24 through 2027-28. Operational Boundary (Indicator 5): £100m GF + £188m HRA = £288m total, flat across the same period

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Sections 2.24 and 2.26, page 9. Section 2.24 states 'This Prudential Indicator separately identifies borrowing from other long-term liabilities' but the table shows GF/HRA breakdown only — OLTL is not quantified in the paper. GF Authorised Limit at £110m against forecast actual GF external debt of £0 is £110m of unused headroom every year. HRA Authorised Limit at £188m against forecast actual of £110m by 2027-28 is £78m of headroom on the HRA side.

facts.value: £15m maximum in any single specified organisation; £20m total with any group (£15m max per single member); £50m maximum total invested for more than 365 days. Cash deposits limited to UK Local Authorities, UK Government, Housing Associations and 'high credit quality' institutions (AAA for sterling MMFs, minimum A- for banks/building societies). Council bank HSBC excluded from the £15m limit as a practical necessity

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Sections 3.7-3.14, pages 15-16, and Indicator 10 at 3.15 page 18. In practice tighter: single organisation not more than 20% of overall external investment total. HSBC banking accounts specifically excluded from the £15m limit because cash regularly moves in excess of £15m and instant-access balances have to be tolerated. Restrictive counterparty policy — but consistent with a small district treasury with mostly HSBC and short-dated exposures.

facts.value: Options for prudent MRP set out at Sections 2.44-2.51 (pages 12-14): (1) over estimated asset life via equal instalment method or annuity method, or (2) match to depreciation. Council to assess appropriate option in advance of MRP commencement. HRA excluded from MRP duty per 2.50. Asset-life defaults: Investment Properties and Buildings 50y; Land and Heritage 50y; Vehicles and Equipment 7-15y; IT Equipment 3-10y; Car Parks 25y. No change from prior year MRP methodology disclosed in the paper

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Standard menu, no unusual choices, no override or reclassification declared.

facts.value: Section 2.16-2.17 (page 7) discloses an existing commercial property portfolio not required by the Prudential Code to be sold. Section 2.16 flags that 'should the Council have an expected need to borrow, the Prudential Code requires the Council to review options for exiting commercial property investments where these can be reasonably realised'. Section 2.17 records that PWLB rules allow investment in commercial land and property including repair, renewal and updating of existing commercial properties provided this does not limit PWLB access. No portfolio size, valuation or income figure printed in this appendix

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: Guildford has been notable in the sector for its commercial property portfolio and subsidiary company arrangements. The paper acknowledges the review obligation without quantifying the position — the numbers would sit in the Asset Investment Strategy at Appendix 3 (s42513, not read for this note).

facts.value: DOES NOT TIE. Their forecast Actual Gross Debt at 31 March 2026 is £131m, all HRA (Section 2.20, page 8). No loan-count, no weighted rate and no maturity schedule is printed for comparison. Our price_book.py 'GUILDFORD BOROUGH COUNCIL' returns: 0 loans at 2025-11-01; 2 loans / £30m at 4.3367% at 2025-12-01; 4 loans / £65m at 4.2815% at 2026-01-20 (meeting date); 21 loans / £289,962,273 at 3.7965% at 2026-03-31 (year end) — and remains at 21 loans / £289.96m today (2026-08-15). Zero loans outstanding in our file at any date on or before 2025-11-01

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.value: Paper's own '-Under/over external borrowing' line at Section 2.20: -£27m in 2023-24 actual, -£41m in 2024-25 estimate, -£52m in 2025-26 estimate, -£76m in 2026-27 estimate, -£81m in 2027-28 estimate. Deepens each year — three-fold over the five-year window

source.title: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Appendix 2 to Capital Strategy 2026/27 report (s42510)

facts.note: This is the total under-borrowed position across GF and HRA together. Composition changes over the forecast: at 2025-26 the £52m under is roughly £22m GF (its whole CFR) + £29m HRA (CFR £160m minus external £131m). By 2027-28 the £81m under is £40m GF (its whole CFR) + £40m HRA. So over the forecast period the GF and HRA converge at roughly £40m each of internal-funded CFR. Section 2.40 explicitly flags the stance as prudent under current cash-return and counterparty conditions.

officer.subject: Your General Fund carries no external PWLB debt through 2027-28
officer.meeting: Overview & Scrutiny Committee 20 January 2026 and Executive 29 January 2026 (both past). Next natural treasury item is the mid-year debt monitoring report — no future date is fixed on the current appendix.

courses_named: Liability Benchmark: using it in practice
MRP — policy options and revenue impact
PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator
officer.body:
Dear Jo,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since the strategy was set. So below are a couple of thoughts on the Treasury Management Strategy taken to Overview & Scrutiny on 20 January and on to the Executive on 29 January. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The strategy is clearly laid out and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The shape of the plan that stood out reading it is that the General Fund carries no external PWLB debt at all — Indicator 3 at Section 2.20 shows £0 of General Fund external debt at 1 April in every one of the five years shown, and every pound of external borrowing is Housing Revenue Account self-financing from March 2012. The plan keeps it that way through 2027-28. On your own numbers the under-borrowed position widens each year — the '-Under/over external borrowing' line runs -£27m at 31 March 2024, -£41m in 2025, -£52m in 2026, -£76m in 2027 and -£81m by 31 March 2028. Section 2.40 flags the stance explicitly as prudent while cash returns are low and counterparty risk uncertain. Not many councils we've read carry the General Fund entirely on internal cash across a five-year strategy — worth noting as a distinctive structural stance.

The maturity indicator at Section 2.32 caught our eye too. Setting the upper limit equal to the lower limit at every bucket — 31%, 44%, 23%, 2% — removes any discretion for you to move the profile during the year without going offside on both sides at once. Most councils we've read write a band. On a book that is largely a single 2012 settlement pool that reads as deliberate rather than accidental, and worth flagging as a distinctive stance rather than anything to act on.

One small piece of arithmetic worth being clear about before members read Indicator 8 in isolation. Your HRA financing-cost line at Indicator 7 rises by roughly £1m per year across the forecast (£12.3m to £16.4m) even as HRA gross external debt falls from £150m to £110m. That looks counter-intuitive on its own. It ties to the paragraph 2.30 definition of financing costs, which includes principal repayment — so the rising line reflects the amortisation charge climbing as more of the 2012 pool comes due each year, not any new borrowing. It pushes Indicator 8's HRA ratio from 38% to 46% of net revenue stream over the same period. The mechanism reads cleanly from the numbers you print, but the two lines going in opposite directions is one members sometimes ask about.

We price every published PWLB book daily against the DMO's premature-repayment curve at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis — indicative only, and only the DMO can quote. We should note that our loan file for Guildford does not currently reconcile cleanly to your published external position, which is a data-quality issue on our side we're working on; disclosing it because we'd rather flag it than gloss it, but not asking you to act on it.

One standing point because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151: the liability benchmark pathway becomes central, and an interactive version is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity. Your Indicator 6 chart on page 10 is compact — the four underlying series (existing loan debt, forecast net loan debt, CFR and gross loans requirement) are the ones the code updates will lean on.

On training, three fit the paper. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice picks up Indicator 6. MRP — policy options and revenue impact covers the methodology at 2.44 to 2.51. PWLB break costs — mechanics & live calculator sits behind any conversation about the shape of the HRA amortisation schedule. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if any of it is useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Appendix 2 to the Capital Strategy 2026/27 report), Overview & Scrutiny Committee 20 January 2026, at https://democracy.guildford.gov.uk/documents/s42512/item-6-appendix-2-treasury-management-strategy.pdf, with the covering report at https://democracy.guildford.gov.uk/documents/s42510/item-6-capital-strategy-2026-27-report.pdf.
